chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and said to him:
How many wives may a slave marry?
He said: My father عليه السلام said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “He may not exceed two wives.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh; Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.أَبِي: my father; referring to the preceding Imam in the chain
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the slave; a bondsman whose marriage limit is being discussed
key_terms.امْرَأَتَيْنِ: two wives; the stated upper limit
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام
key_terms.لَا يَزِيدُ: he does not exceed; indicating a legal maximum
key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجُ: to marry; here, the legal capacity to contract marriage

ai.seo_question: How many wives can a slave marry according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning marriage for a slave, stating that he may not marry more than two wives. It is presented through a chain from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, through his father, from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, reflecting a jurisprudential limit in marriage law.
